title: Velocity at B
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the speed at point B as 4 m/s using Newton's second law for circular motion and the given normal force.

title: Horizontal Distance BC
description: Essential: Correctly determines the horizontal range from B to C as 3.2 m using projectile motion equations and the given height difference.

title: Time to Max Distance
description: Essential: Correctly finds the time after leaving B to reach the point farthest from the incline as 0.4 s, using the geometry of the projectile's velocity relative to the slope.

title: Force Balance at B
description: Important: Applies Newton's second law at point B, relating normal force, weight, centripetal force, and speed.

title: Projectile Motion Setup
description: Important: Correctly models the motion after B as projectile motion with initial horizontal velocity and identifies the landing condition on the incline.

title: Geometry of Incline
description: Important: Uses the relationship between the horizontal range, vertical drop, and the slope of the track BC to set up the correct equation for the landing point.

title: Distance from Track
description: Optional: Correctly formulates the perpendicular distance from the projectile to the line BC as a function of time to find its maximum.

title: Sign or Direction Error
description: Pitfall: Misapplies the sign of forces at point B (e.g., adding weight and normal force incorrectly for centripetal force) or misinterprets the direction of the normal force.

title: Projectile Equation Error
description: Pitfall: Uses incorrect kinematic equations for the projectile phase, such as wrong sign for gravitational acceleration or misrelating horizontal and vertical displacements.
